newsitem.title: UK: Five killed as gales, torrential rain lash Britain.
newsitem.headline: Five killed as gales, torrential rain lash Britain.

text.p: Five people were killed and several injured when fierce gales and torrential rain lashed Britain overnight, emergency services said on Thursday.
The London Weather Centre said the gales reached up to 80 miles (130 km) per hour in some parts of Britain.

Three members of a four-man crew were killed when their yacht capsized in heavy seas whipped up by strong winds off the Isle of Wight on the southern English coast. The fourth crew member was rescued.
A mother and her eight-year-old daughter died in a car crash when she swerved to avoid a fallen tree at Fallingroyd in northern England.
Police and other emergency services reported a spate of injuries due to fallen trees, vehicles blown across roads and damage to houses.

Southampton airport in southern England was closed after a plane carrying 30 passengers and three crew burst two tyres on impact with the runway as the pilots battled against the strong winds. No one was injured.
A passenger aircraft on a flight from London was forced to abort two landing attempts at Glasgow airport in Scotland because of the gales before finally touching down.
The stormy weather also forced the cancellation of all ferry services between Northern Ireland and Scotland.
Some major road bridges were closed because of the danger of vehicles being blown over the side. Flood warnings were issued in several areas.
